title: usenet-ipfs-mail: JMAP daemon for mail-client access to Usenet content
description:
Why: standard newsreader clients (slrn, tin, Thunderbird NNTP mode) are well served by usenet-ipfs-reader. But mobile mail clients (iOS Mail, Android Gmail, Fastmail) and modern web clients have no NNTP support and are adding JMAP (RFC 8620/8621). A JMAP interface over the same IPFS article store would let any mail client browse Usenet groups without modification.

Why JMAP and not IMAP: JMAP is HTTP/JSON, cleaner to implement, naturally content-addressed (blobId maps to CID), and has a push model (SSE/WebSocket) rather than IMAP IDLE. Mobile clients are gaining JMAP support. IMAP adds ~100-command protocol complexity and long-lived stateful TCP connections with no corresponding benefit over JMAP.

Workspace addition: new crate usenet-ipfs-mail (bin + lib), imports usenet-ipfs-core for IPFS block access, MsgIdMap, group log. Has its own SQLite tables for per-user state. Does NOT share process or port with usenet-ipfs-reader.

Key mapping decisions (to be designed in sub-issues):
  - Newsgroup -> JMAP Mailbox object
  - Article -> JMAP Email object
  - Article CID -> JMAP blobId (content-addressed, stable)
  - Per-user flags (\Seen, \Flagged) -> new user_flags SQLite table (not in core)
  - POST via JMAP Email/set create -> signs and writes to IPFS via core pipeline
  - Group subscription -> per-user Mailbox subscriptions table

Explicitly out of scope for this epic: IMAP, POP3, ActiveSync, proprietary push APIs.
notes: Deferred: implement only after usenet-ipfs-reader and usenet-ipfs-transit are stable and the HeaderMapNode schema (stoa-1c76e14c) is complete. The structured header map (subject, from, date as RFC 3339) makes the JMAP Email object mapping straightforward — date is already parsed, no MIME header decoding needed at the JMAP layer.
design: Separate binary (usenet-ipfs-mail). HTTP server (axum or hyper). JMAP session endpoint per RFC 8620 §2. Core session discovery at /.well-known/jmap. Email/get, Email/query, Email/set (POST only), Mailbox/get, Mailbox/query. Blob/get returns raw article bytes by CID. Per-user state in SQLite, separate from reader and transit databases. TLS via rustls (same pattern as reader).
